title: Side-channel: crypto delegation to RustCrypto is correct
description:
This is a positive finding (no issue). All cryptographic operations are correctly delegated to RustCrypto crates:

1. Signature verification: pkix-path's SignatureVerifier trait delegates to p256::ecdsa, p384::ecdsa, and rsa crates. The library never performs signature comparison itself -- it calls the RustCrypto verify() methods which handle constant-time comparison internally.

2. OCSP ResponderId byKey matching (pkix-revocation/src/ocsp.rs:486-489): SHA-1 digest comparison uses standard == on hash output bytes. This is NOT a secret comparison -- both the expected hash and the response's KeyHash are derived from public keys, so timing leakage of public certificate content is not a concern.

3. CertID hash comparison (pkix-revocation/src/ocsp.rs:221-222): Same analysis -- issuerNameHash and issuerKeyHash are derived from public certificate fields; byte-equal comparison is correct.

4. DN comparison (pkix-path: names_match): Compares public certificate subject/issuer names. Not secret data.

5. Serial number comparison: Public certificate field.

No instance of secret-dependent comparison, branching on secret bytes, or secret-indexed table lookup was found. The library holds no private key material. All comparisons are over public certificate data.

Location: workspace-wide
